scope: The eight D-class layout issues recorded in artifacts/phase-ui-seekgt-final-visual/visual-comparison.md. No redesign, no new UI goals.
measurementNote: Before values are from the round-4 final-visual audit, taken at commit 00dd6cf. After values are DOM measurements taken at the same viewports after the fix. No pixel comparison against a reference image was performed.

findings.issue: Chinese section headings broke mid-compound at 1920
findings.beforeMeasurement: "为开发者打造，全程可观测" 44px, 2 lines in a 502px column. "两种请求格式，一个统一管控的网关" rendered as ["两种请求格式，一", "个统一管控的网关"] — split inside the compound 一个.
findings.rootCause: Two independent causes. (1) In `side` mode the title sat in a 0.8fr column that resolved to 502px at both 1440 and 1920, because --container-content caps at 84rem, while type-section-title kept growing with vw (42px -> 44px). (2) Chinese has no inter-word spaces, so once a heading wraps the break can land between any two glyphs, and `text-wrap: balance` actively aimed for the midpoint.
findings.afterMeasurement: Column ratio inverted to 1.15fr/0.85fr and heading max-width raised to max-w-3xl: "为开发者打造，全程可观测" is 1 line at 1280/1440/1920. "两种请求格式，..." is 1 line at 1280/1440 and at 1920 breaks as ["两种请求格式，", "一个统一管控的网关"] — at the comma. `word-break: keep-all` with `overflow-wrap: anywhere` as the escape hatch.
findings.acceptanceResult: PASS — no mid-compound break at any tested width; no heading overflow; asserted by 'D1: Chinese section headings never break mid-compound at 1920'.

findings.issue: Pricing rendered two cards into a three-column grid
findings.beforeMeasurement: gridTemplateColumns "416px 416px 416px" with 2 cards; cards spanned 848 of 1280 available; 432px (34%) empty on the right; identical at both widths.
findings.rootCause: `md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3` was applied unconditionally, independent of how many results exist. The catalogue had been fixed in round 4 with inline logic; pricing was missed and the logic was not shared.
findings.afterMeasurement: Pricing: "566px 566px", cards span 1152 of 1280, 64px empty left AND 64px right — centred, not left-hugging. Catalogue unchanged at "486px 486px", span 992/992, 0px empty. Both now call the shared resultGridClass(count).
findings.acceptanceResult: PASS — column count never exceeds card count; asserted by 'D2: two results never render into a three-column grid' across both routes. No placeholder card added.

findings.issue: Sign-in was mostly empty background at tablet portrait
findings.beforeMeasurement: aside display:none (it was lg:flex, and 768 < 1024). Card 342px inside 960px main = 36% fill, with 309px dead space above and 309px below.
findings.rootCause: The narrative column existed only from `lg`, and the form column kept `items-center`, so between 768 and 1023 a lone card floated in an empty column.
findings.afterMeasurement: sign-in 768x1024: narrative visible as a band above the form, 369px + 342px card = 74% fill. sign-up 768x1024: 78%. 820x1180: 71%. 1024x768: side-by-side, 100%. 390x844: narrative hidden, form first, no overflow.
findings.acceptanceResult: PASS — >60% fill at 768 on both routes, form-first preserved at 390; asserted by the two D3 tests. No auth logic, OAuth, Passkey, captcha, forgot-password, redirect or Session behaviour touched.

findings.issue: Leaderboard masthead used a bespoke type scale
findings.beforeMeasurement: h1 used a one-off clamp(1.75rem, 4vw, 2.5rem) that existed nowhere else, so the leaderboard title rendered visibly smaller than every other page title.
findings.rootCause: The component predated the shared typography tokens and was never migrated.
findings.afterMeasurement: Uses the shared type-page-title plus the standard eyebrow and lede treatment; h1 font-size now equals the catalogue's h1 to within 1px.
findings.acceptanceResult: PASS — asserted by 'D4: leaderboard masthead uses the shared page-title scale', which compares against /model-catalog rather than a literal value. Left alignment deliberately retained: the reference leaderboard is left-aligned.

findings.issue: Two dates rendered as two giant slabs
findings.beforeMeasurement: Visual: each bar occupied roughly 30% of the chart width, so the panel read as a broken graphic rather than a sparse one. Not DOM-measurable — see limitation below.
findings.rootCause: A band scale divides the plot area by category count, so at two categories each bar takes half the plot minus padding. No maximum bar width was configured.
findings.afterMeasurement: barMaxWidth: 64 on both the models history and market share specs. The cap only binds at low cardinality; at 7, 30 or 365 points the natural width is already below it, so denser periods are unaffected.
findings.acceptanceResult: PARTIAL — the change is applied and verified in the after screenshots, but there is NO automated assertion. VChart renders to <canvas>, so bar geometry is not readable from the DOM; a screenshot-diff would be the only automated check and none is set up. This is the one item in this round without a regression test, and it is called out rather than glossed. No data point was added, removed or interpolated.

findings.issue: About masthead was outside the public page system
findings.beforeMeasurement: Container padding `py-16 sm:py-24`, against pricing's `pt-16 pb-12 sm:pt-20 sm:pb-16` and the catalogue's `pt-24 pb-16 sm:pt-28` — three public pages, three different vertical rhythms.
findings.rootCause: Each page set its own masthead padding; only pricing had been tuned (in round 4).
findings.afterMeasurement: About, pricing and the catalogue all use `pt-16 pb-12 sm:pt-20 sm:pb-16`. About already used the shared type-label/type-page-title tokens, so only the container rhythm changed.
findings.acceptanceResult: PASS — left-aligned product narrative retained deliberately; New API attribution, AGPL and the upstream repository link are unchanged.

findings.issue: Section spacing was excessive on large screens
findings.beforeMeasurement: section-block was clamp(4rem, 8vw, 7.5rem): 102px a side at 1280, 115px at 1440, 120px at 1920 — i.e. 205px, 230px and 240px between adjacent sections.
findings.rootCause: The 8vw coefficient and 7.5rem ceiling were set for a narrower container and never revisited when the container widened to 84rem.
findings.afterMeasurement: clamp(4rem, 5.2vw, 5.25rem): 67px/134px at 1280, 75px/150px at 1440, 84px/168px at 1920. The 4rem floor is unchanged, so 390 and 768 keep exactly their previous 128px gap.
findings.acceptanceResult: PASS — every large width lands inside the 128–176px band; asserted by 'D7: section rhythm at large widths stays inside the intended band'. Small screens provably unaffected.

findings.issue: Capability panels and the three-step row were under-weighted at 1920
findings.beforeMeasurement: Wide (col-span-7) and narrow (col-span-5) panels used identical internals: p-6, text-base title, text-sm body, text-xs index. The step markers were size-12 circles with size-5 glyphs against roughly 240px of surrounding whitespace.
findings.rootCause: The grid expressed hierarchy through span only; nothing expressed it through type or density, so at 1920 the section read as 1440 content stretched across a wider canvas.
findings.afterMeasurement: PublicFeaturePanel gained an explicit `emphasis` flag, set on the two col-span-7 panels: title text-lg/xl/2xl versus text-base/lg, body lg:text-base, padding p-6/lg:p-7/xl:p-8. Steps: marker size-12 -> lg:size-16, glyph size-5 -> lg:size-7, title text-base -> lg:text-xl, body lg:text-base, copy width max-w-xs -> lg:max-w-sm. All steps are lg-gated, so 390 and 768 are unchanged.
findings.acceptanceResult: PASS on the structural claim — the primary/secondary distinction is now explicit in the component API rather than implied by span. Whether the resulting weight matches the reference is a visual judgement and is NOT claimed here.

notReclaimed: No pixel-level comparison was performed. The SeekGT reference screenshots were not available to this session — they are not stored in the repository and did not survive context compaction. Statements about the reference are second-hand from docs/phase-ui-seekgt-alignment.md.
D5 has no automated regression test because VChart renders to canvas.
Sparsity on the leaderboard, catalogue and pricing pages is unchanged and is a real data-volume limit: two models, two days of history. Nothing was padded.
